item.title: Caitlin Clark, Fever get absolute reality check in Game 1 playoff beatdown against Aces
item.description: A'ja Wilson's 38-point, 16-rebound masterclass powered the Las Vegas Aces to a dominant 102-85 Game 1 rout over the Indiana Fever in playoffs.
item.content:encoded:
The Indiana Fever limped into the postseason with zero momentum after getting blown out by 20 points against the Minnesota Lynx in their regular-season finale, and Sunday's playoff opener offered little hope.

In Game 1 of their best-of-three first-round series, the Las Vegas Aces put on a clinic, strong-arming Indy in a 102-85 rout.

Having proven they could beat the defending champions during the regular season, Indiana fans hoped to make a statement early. Instead, Las Vegas stepped on the gas from the opening tip and built a lead as large as 27 points, leaving Indiana scrambling to stay afloat for nearly the entire second half.

INDIANA FEVER ROUTED BY LYNX IN REGULAR SEASON FINALE AS CAITLIN CLARK POSTS CAREER-WORST PERFORMANCE

Las Vegas was led by a dominant performance from MVP-hopeful A'ja Wilson, who was virtually unstoppable and carried the Aces on both ends of the floor. Wilson finished with 38 points and 16 rebounds. Yet the primary story of the game was Indiana's inability to execute against a physical and disciplined playoff defense.

Indiana's backcourt spent the afternoon fighting through traps and relentless double teams.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Caitlin Clark worked her way to a double-double, racking up 15 points, 10 assists and three rebounds.

But the Aces hounded her and disrupted her shooting rhythm throughout the day. Clark made just 6 of 18 shots, including 3 from deep — committing six turnovers and picking up five fouls. Kelsey Mitchell struggled to find her scoring rhythm, too. She finished with 12 points and three assists, connecting on only 4-of-16.

FEVER'S SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WEARS SENSATIONAL CHEETAH-PRINT OUTFIT AHEAD OF PLAYOFF GAME VS ACES

With their two primary creators unable to find their rhythm, the Fever lacked the offensive firepower needed to trade baskets with a red-hot Vegas squad. Aliyah Boston led the Fever with 18 points, adding eight rebounds and dishing out four assists.

Off the bench, Sophie Cunningham provided a much-needed spark for the Fever. Cunningham scored 13 points, including three shots from beyond the arc. She offered Indiana a spark during a tough second half, but it wasn't enough to mount a real threat.

Game 2 of the series shifts home to Indianapolis Tuesday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. The Fever will desperately be looking to protect their home court to keep their season alive and force a Game 3.

item.title: Phillies avoid collapse, Astros sneak in as MLB Postseason is set
item.description: Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper powered the Philadelphia Phillies past the Tampa Bay Rays to clinch a wild-card berth on the season's final day.
item.content:encoded:
The chill is in the air, the days of summer feel long gone already, the weather is changing, the leaves are falling and it could only mean that one thing is on the horizon – postseason baseball.

The field was set on Sunday as baseball fans had their eyes on a handful of teams. The Philadelphia Phillies needed a win to get in and avoid a devastating collapse and the Houston Astros just needed a victory to clinch their spot in the playoffs.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Luckily, for both teams, disaster was averted.

Kyle Schwarber’s two-run double and Bryce Harper’s solo home run propelled the Phillies to a 7-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays. It gave Philadelphia a wild-card berth as the team finished 88-74 on the year.

Philadelphia had lost six of its last eight games before Sunday's win.

Houston just needed a win to wrap up the American League West division title. The Astros responded with a 9-0 victory over the Athletics in Sacramento. Ethan Pecko gave Houston three innings of strong work, allowing only one hit and striking out two. The rest of the bullpen did its job to close the door. Christian Walker hit his 29th home run of the season in the sixth to bolster the Astros’ chances.

The Astros finished the year 81-81.

October baseball will finally be upon us after a wild season.

The American League division winners include the Tampa Bay Rays (AL East), Cleveland Guardians (AL Central) and the Astros (AL West). The National League division winners include the Atlanta Braves (NL East), Milwaukee Brewers (NL Central) and Los Angeles Dodgers (NL West).

The Rays, Guardians, Brewers and Dodgers each have a bye into the Division Series.

The Wild Card portion of the bracket begins Tuesday. The Braves take on the Phillies, the Astros meet the Chicago White Sox, the New York Yankees go up against the Boston Red Sox and the San Diego Padres and Chicago Cubs battle it out.

The Wild Card round is a best-of-three. The Phillies and Braves begin the postseason at 2 p.m. ET on Tuesday.

item.title: Florida Gators, Mississippi State soar, USC tumbles in latest inexplicable AP Top 25 Poll
item.description: The Florida Gators surged 13 spots to No. 8 in the AP Top 25 poll after demolishing Ole Miss, while Missouri's puzzling ranking fuels SEC bias debate.
item.content:encoded:
One of college football's greatest traditions got another entry on Sunday, as the week four edition of the AP Top 25 Poll was released to mostly bemused reactions from confused fans.

And if there was any doubt that the SEC continues to enjoy some, uh, questionable, benefits based on preseason polling and perceived strength, this week's voting should put that to rest.

Unsurprisingly, one of the biggest gainers of the week was the Florida Gators, coming off an impressive 52-28 win over the Ole Miss Rebels. Florida racked up over 300 yards on the ground, forced two turnovers, and kept the ball away from Trinidad Chambliss and the powerful Ole Miss offense. After what could be a season-changing win, the Gators moved up a whopping 13 spots to No. 8, one spot ahead of the Rebels.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Oklahoma State Cowboys were another big mover, jumping 11 spots to No. 19, as their win over the Oregon Ducks looks even better after OU's win over USC. UCLA , too, moved 14 spots into the top 25 at No. 23 thanks to a 54-3 obliteration of the Maryland Terrapins. Another surprise team through week four? The Mississippi State Bulldogs, who held on to beat Missouri and moved up eight spots to No. 16.

But speaking of Missouri, they exemplify the problem that the preseason poll and voters' pre-conceived biases have with these rankings.

The Tigers entered the season as the No. 25 team in the preseason poll and proceeded to do literally nothing of importance in the first three weeks. A 54-21 win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff, a 38-21 win over a bad Kansas team, and a surprisingly close 27-17 win over an atrocious Troy team.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Their reward was to move up to No. 19 heading into the game against the Bulldogs, which resulted in the 31-24 loss. Somehow, after again, looking very unimpressive for the entirety of the season, Missouri sits at ... No. 25 in the week four poll. That's the exact type of SEC-specific outcome that fans from other conferences complain about. Look bad, do nothing, lose, stay right where you were. And then brag about the number of "ranked games" and "ranked wins."

Meanwhile, Missouri has not beaten an SEC team that finished the season with a winning record since 2024 and their wins that season were over 7-6 Arkansas and 7-6 Vanderbilt.

DAN LANNING BLASTS USC AFTER OREGON'S WIN, AS LINCOLN RILEY OFFICIALLY ENTERS HOT SEAT IN LA

Meanwhile, Kentucky moved up three spots to No. 24, even though their win over Texas A&M looks far less impressive than it did a week ago, with the Aggies looking more like a top 50 team this year than top 25. But the Missouri ranking has immense value, as it means their upcoming game against Florida is yet another "ranked matchup in the SEC."

Meanwhile, Iowa, who pulled up the upset win over Michigan with a last-second touchdown, moves up just three spots. Michigan went from No. 18 to unranked. Penn State dropped from No. 13 to unranked after losing to Wisconsin, who had a miraculous late touchdown pass of their own in Happy Valley, and USC fell six spots after losing to Oregon.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Nebraska is unranked because they started the preseason unranked, while advanced metric systems put the Cornhuskers at No. 16 based on their actual performance. Wake Forest beat No. 16 Louisville on the road, and their one loss was to a top-five Miami team, but they're unranked while Missouri is. There's no logic or consistency to any of it, it's just a grab bag based on eye test, preseason polls, conference affiliation, the size of a team's stadium and whatever ESPN chooses to highlight.

Here's the full poll:

Again, the upside is that the AP Poll at the end of the day doesn't matter. The downside? There's no doubt that these awful rankings are used to inform the College Football Playoff selection committee's deliberations and provide fodder for "strength of schedule" and "strength of conference" and "resume wins" arguments and so on. Texas A&M, despite currently sitting at No. 39 in computer-based rankings, one spot ahead of UCF, will count as a "ranked win" for Kentucky and LSU, because preseason polls expected them to be good. They are not good.

With a full slate of big games in week five, expect more AP absurdity to come next week. After all, it's one of the sport's most cherished traditions.

item.title: Top NFL Draft prospect receives indefinite suspension after outburst in loss to Alabama
item.description: Dylan Stewart's indefinite suspension goes beyond the punch that got him ejected, says South Carolina's Shane Beamer, raising questions about the top prospect's future.
item.content:encoded:
Read almost every 2027 NFL mock draft and South Carolina Gamecocks edge rusher Dylan Stewart is predicted to be at least a top-10 pick.

An incident on Saturday is expected to raise more questions than answers.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Stewart was ejected from South Carolina’s 49-14 loss to the Alabama Crimson Tide after he punched tight end Josh Ford’s helmet. He then argued with coaches on the sideline.

All of that resulted in an indefinite suspension on Sunday. South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer announced the punishment during a press conference.

"I'll make the decision on what his future looks like beyond this week here in the next day or so. Still having some meetings and talking with him, but he won't play this week versus Kentucky. There's a standard of how we do things in our program and that was not it last night," Beamer said, via 247 Sports. "It's beyond the punch. The punch is unacceptable.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"He's not the first person to ever throw a punch in the football game and he won't be the last. But it's some of the other stuff. That isn't how we do things in this program. Accountability is a core value in this program and we are all accountable to the standard, so we'll see what that looks like here going forward."

Stewart burst onto the scene during his freshman year. He had 6.5 sacks and 23 total tackles in 2024. In 2025, Stewart had 4.5 sacks and 33 total tackles.

He was a second-team All-SEC selection as voted on by coaches last year. College football expert Phil Steele also named him an honorable mention All-American.

It’s unclear when or if Stewart will return to the field this season.

South Carolina fell to 2-2 with the loss against Alabama. The Gamecocks are set to take on Kentucky this coming Saturday.

item.title: 'Home Improvement' star says Patricia Richardson got 'tired' of fighting for sitcom
item.description: Taran Noah Smith reveals Patricia Richardson fought to keep "Home Improvement" realistic as new writers pushed scripts in a different direction.
item.content:encoded:
"Home Improvement" star Taran Noah Smith is shedding new light on why the hit 1990s sitcom came to an end.

The 42-year-old former actor was seven-years-old when he landed the role of Mark Taylor, the youngest son of Tim "The Tool Man" Taylor (Tim Allen) and his wife Jill Taylor (Patricia Richardson) in 1991.

The sitcom, which was based on Allen's stand-up comedy persona, centered on Tim, a television host known for his home improvement show, "Tool Time," and his family life with Jill, Mark and older sons Brad (Zachery Ty Bryan) and Randy (Jonathan Taylor Thomas).

'HOME IMPROVEMENT' STAR JONATHAN TAYLOR THOMAS ARRESTED FOR ALLEGED PUBLIC INTOXICATION, RESISTING DEPUTY

"Home Improvement" became one of the highest-rated shows of the '90s and ran for eight seasons and aired 204 episodes. However, the show concluded in 1999 after Richardson declined to return for a proposed ninth season.

During a recent appearance on Tom Scharpling and Julia Vickerman's podcast "Outgrown" podcast, Smith reflected on his time starring on the show and weighed in on the reasons behind Richardson's departure.

TIM ALLEN SAYS HE 'NEVER REALLY WANTED' TO BE A DAD AND OPENS UP ABOUT SOBRIETY AND FATHERHOOD REGRETS

Smith recalled that Richardson joined the cast as Jill just days before the pilot was taped after producers replaced Frances Fisher, the actress originally cast as Tim's wife, during rehearsals.

"When they brought Patricia in, there was just a much better chemistry," he said. "And she had her own kid. She had just given birth to twins, and she had one older kid who was about my age. She really brought a lot more of a realistic mom energy to her, and she fought throughout the whole show to keep the show more realistic."

"She would tell the writers, ‘A mother would never say this,’ and get them to change it," he added.

Smith said he "definitely" agreed with Richardson's input though he acknowledged that he and the show's other child stars weren't really involved in conversations about the script.

"They'd do a run-through of the script on Monday and then the kids would go to school usually, and they would continue to discuss the script," he said.

Smith recalled that there were creative disagreements on set after a new creative team replaced the show's original writers and producers.

ROSEANNE BARR HASN’T SPOKEN TO TV SISTER LAURIE METCALF SINCE SHOW’S CANCELLATION

"The original creators only did the first couple seasons, and then they moved on, and they brought in a whole other group of writer/producers," he remembered. "Those guys, very few of them had kids, and the show kind of started to go in a different direction, at least the scripts we'd get on Monday."

"It was really Pat, the mom, who fought the good fight to make it more realistic because oftentimes it would just be something that was very out of character just to sell a joke, just to set up a joke," he continued. "It's like, ‘Wait, this is not what the characters are about.’"

ROSEANNE BARR CALLS FORMER CO-STAR A 'BRAINWASHED BIGOT' AFTER HE SAID REBOOT WAS 'RIGHTFULLY CANCELED'

Smith speculated that Allen was reluctant to appear overly controlling after witnessing what happened on another sitcom, "Roseanne." "Roseanne," which became an instant hit after it premiered in 1988, was created by "Home Improvement" co-creator Matt Williams. Like "Home Improvement," Roseanne was built around its star's stand-up comedy voice and persona.

However, Barr clashed behind-the-scenes with producers and writers, including Williams, over the direction and tone of the show. The tensions between the two led to Williams leaving after the first season. Barr later gained more influence and was credited as a creator in later seasons.

‘THE OFFICE’ STAR JENNA FISCHER EXPOSES THE GRUELING REALITY THAT FORCED HER OFF TV

"I think Tim was overall maybe a bit worried about being a tyrant because the same creators created ‘Roseanne,’ and Roseanne took over the show and fired the creators, fired everybody," Smith recalled. "Actually, all our camera crew had been fired in one day from ‘Roseanne’ and came over to us. So, Tim was always, I think, more hands-off with that, not wanting to be tyrannical, which meant that it was a lot more on Pat to push."

"That's one of the reasons why the show ended up eventually ending, because she was just tired of it, of having to fight to make it realistic all the time," he continued.

JODIE SWEETIN SHARES SHOCKING 'FULL HOUSE' RESIDUAL CHECK AMOUNT DESPITE SHOW'S MEGA SUCCESS

"And Tim was getting far more money than she was," Smith added. "That was her actual way of stopping. She said she'd do a ninth season if she got paid the same amount as Tim, knowing they wouldn't do it."

Smith's recollection of why Richardson left "Home Improvement" echoes what the actress has said for years about her experience on the show and the reasons for her departure.

During a May 2024 interview with the Los Angeles Times, Richardson recalled that the creators emphasized the importance of the character of Jill and her relationship with Tim.

"When I took the job, they said it wasn’t meant to be the Tim Allen show. It was meant to be our show," she said. "I’ve always said, I don’t want to play the thankless wife."

Richardson recalled having creative disagreements with male writers over how Jill would react to specific situations, remembering one instance in which she was told, "Pat, it’s not like we don’t understand women. We’re married to them."

The actress, who earned four Primetime Emmy Award nominations for her performance as Jill, told the LA Times that she made the decision to leave the show.

Richardson told the LA Times she decided during the eighth season that it would be her last, citing a desire to spend more time with her children after her divorce and her belief that the sitcom had run its course, pointing to Jonathan Taylor Thomas' departure and declining ratings.

The actress also felt that Disney failed to recognize her creative contributions to the series, saying she helped shape her character and storylines but was denied a producer credit, even as Allen became an executive producer.

"I told everybody, there’s not enough money in the world to get me to do a ninth year. This show is over. It needs to end," Richardson recalled.

Richardson recalled that ABC unexpectedly offered to continue the show with a 25-episode ninth season. She said the network's parent company, Disney, proposed paying her a salary of $1 million an episode, while Allen would be paid $2 million an episode.

Though she recalled Allen immediately accepting the offer, she said she countered with terms that she knew the studio would reject. Richardson told the outlet that she requested equal pay with Allen and an executive producer credit.

"I knew that Disney would in no way pay me that much. That was my way to say ‘no’ and was a little bit of a flip-off to Disney," Richardson said. "I’d been there all this time, and they never even paid me a third of what Tim was making, and I was working my a-- off. I was a big reason why women were watching."

item.title: Susie Wiles reveals brutal toll of fighting cancer while running Trump’s White House
item.description: Susie Wiles reveals what it was like to undergo chemotherapy while leading the White House staff, saying some days just getting out of bed was a test.
item.content:encoded:
White House chief of staff Susie Wiles is opening up about the grueling reality of fighting breast cancer while holding one of Washington's most demanding jobs, revealing that some days simply getting out of bed and going to work took all the strength she had.

In an op-ed published Sunday in USA Today, Wiles described what it was like to undergo chemotherapy while continuing to lead the White House staff for President Donald Trump. 

The disease occupied her thoughts from the moment she woke up and sometimes even while she slept, she wrote.

"Fighting cancer is brutal and unrelenting," Wiles wrote. Questions about treatment, test results and what might come next could overtake even a strong mind. At times, she acknowledged, they overtook hers.

CANCER-RELATED BRAIN FOG MAY IMPROVE WITH 2 SIMPLE TREATMENTS, SCIENTISTS SAY

Some days, Wiles said, she poured her strength into fighting the disease. On others, getting out of bed, getting dressed and going to work was its own test. "Most days, I carried the full weight of both," she wrote.

Work gave her a purpose beyond appointments, scans and side effects. "Cancer can make your world very small," Wiles wrote. She said she pushed herself to stay focused on the people who depended on her, even as she knew others might question whether she could still lead effectively.

KAI TRUMP REVEALS HOW FAMILY RALLIED AROUND MOM VANESSA AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE: ‘IT’S A LONG JOURNEY’

The treatment did take a toll on her stamina, mobility and, at times, her focus. Wiles said she could not always be everywhere she wanted to be. Colleagues inside and outside the White House stepped in, while her two daughters, extended family, friends and medical team helped carry her through the illness.

Wiles made clear that working through treatment would not be right or possible for everyone. For her, she wrote, the job helped her hold on to a sense of who she was beyond the disease.

CANCER SURVIVORS MAY SEE SURPRISING BENEFITS FROM ONE SPECIFIC EXERCISE, STUDY SAYS

After successful surgery, pathology showed no residual cancer, Wiles wrote. She said she now faces the work of rebuilding what treatment took from her.

"Chemotherapy is, in a word, a b----," she wrote.

DOLLY PARTON’S PRIVATE CANCER BATTLE HIGHLIGHTS WHY SOME PATIENTS DON’T SHARE THEIR DIAGNOSES

In a post on X Sunday, Wiles said she rarely writes about herself but wanted to share what it was like to fight cancer while continuing to do a job she loves.

"Cancer tried to make my world smaller. I was determined not to let it," she wrote, adding that she hoped her account could offer strength to someone still fighting the disease.

VANESSA TRUMP REVEALS BREAST CANCER DIAGNOSIS IN EMOTIONAL STATEMENT: 'I AM STAYING FOCUSED AND HOPEFUL'

Wiles announced Sept. 16 that she was cancer free after receiving clear pathology results following an appointment at the Mayo Clinic. She had disclosed her early-stage breast cancer diagnosis in March.

Trump praised Wiles during her treatment, saying in a prerecorded May tribute that she was winning her cancer battle. Wiles thanked him for his kindness and compassion, and credited her family, friends, colleagues and doctors with helping her through the ordeal.

For others going through treatment, Wiles offered a message of hope. "Cancer does not have to take away who you are," she wrote. She said that for her, life beyond the disease includes serving Trump and the country and being a mother, grandmother and friend.

One of those daughters, Katie Wiles, responded to her mother’s account on X. "A strong woman isn’t loud in her strength; she’s steady and unshakable," she wrote. "You are our champion. So incredibly proud of you, Mom."

item.title: Patriots' Drake Maye 'looking myself in the mirror' as game has completely collapsed since AFC Championship
item.description: Drake Maye's three turnovers, raising his season total to seven, prompted Mike Vrabel to pull his quarterback as the Patriots fell 35-6 to the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The collapse of Drake Maye's game continued on Sunday and it was so complete and troubling that coach Mike Vrabel pulled his quarterback with about eight minutes to play.

It was the right move because the Patriots were getting run out of the stadium by the Jacksonville Jaguars, who eventually authored a convincing 35-6 victory.

But it was best for Maye, who accounted for two interceptions and a lost fumble in the game and left Vrabel sounding kind of worried.

DRAKE MAYE'S TERRIBLE DECISION GIFTS SEAHAWKS OPENING NIGHT WIN AS PATRIOTS LEFT STUNNED TO START NFL SEASON

"Well, my concern level is very high for this football team," the coach said.

Vrabel went through the litany of things that he's worried about and that need improvement. But everybody understands that if Maye doesn't stop giving away the football, the other stuff will be secondary.

"We have to take care of the football," Vrabel said. "We can't, we can't force things ... I think he knows what to do. You know what I mean? I think we have to do it better, you know?

"And again, we all want to make plays. We just have to make them good ones. And, if it's not there, we got to make a great decision."

Great decisions do not involve throwing the ball to the other team.

FROM THE CHARGERS TO THE COLTS AND FALCONS, WHICH OF THE NFL'S EIGHT WINLESS TEAMS ARE ALREADY IN PANIC MODE

But Maye's decisions have been questionable.

The three turnovers on Sunday is increasingly typical of how Maye is playing so far this season because he had three in the season-opener against the Seattle Seahawks and had another last week against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

So, seven turnovers by Maye this season.

"The ball stars rolling like that, we can't get out our own way," Maye lamented. "I can't get out of my own way personally.

DRAKE MAYE VOICES SUPPORT FOR PATRIOTS COACH MIKE VRABEL AS OFF-FIELD CONTROVERSY CONTINUES TO SWIRL

"So, I got to look myself in the mirror and take this as a turning point. You know, it's Week 3. We got to, you have some fuel and realize that what we're doing out there offensively is unacceptable – unacceptable for three weeks."

It's good that Maye is looking where the biggest problem is. It means he's a capable leader even at only 24 years old.

"I got to start with myself and then lead these guys and we got to get back after it," he said.

But time is short. The Patriots are 1-2 and already teammates are getting questions about Maye's status in the locker room.

Stunning, but this is the NFL.

"Everybody in that locker room and the organization and in the building believes in him and that's really all that matters," cornerback Christian Gonzalez said. "Obviously, he wants to perform and do that for his team.

"So, with Drake, we're behind him. That's our quarterback. Like I said, this team goes and we ride behind him. So that's our guy and that ain't changing."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Patriots this year are different in that their schedule is more difficult than last year. And the move to release Stefon Diggs and trade for A.J. Brown hasn't paid off because Brown got injured in the season-opener and hasn't played since.

"I mean, listen, the NFL is hard," CBS analyst Adam Archuleta said. "... They're going to have to play their way out of this. And Drake Maye is going to have to play his way out of this."

Archuleta went on to make the point that Maye seemingly raised his game in a game at the Buffalo Bills last year.

The Patriots visit the Bills next Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Irish soccer players wear black armbands, refuse to shake hands ahead of contentious match vs Israel
item.description: Irish players wore black armbands and refused handshakes during the Nations League match against Israel, with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu leaving the team.
item.content:encoded:
Israel and Ireland competed against each other in a highly contentious Nations League match on Sunday in Hungary.

Ireland faced pressure to boycott the match from fans at home over Israel’s response in Gaza following the Oct. 7, 2023, terror attacks committed by Hamas terrorists that left nearly 1,200 people dead.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Ireland’s soccer federation said in June that its home game against Israel was going to be moved to a neutral field with no fans present. It followed the organization’s initial motion to UEFA to ban Israel from club and international play.

Regardless, the efforts to ban Israel were proven futile and the match was played on Sunday in Debrecen.

Irish players made a point to protest, however. The Irish team wore black armbands and looked down at the grass with their hands behind their backs during the playing of the Israeli national anthem.

Ireland’s captain, Dara O’Shea, approached midfield for the pre-match talk with his hands behind his back. He shook hands with the officials but made no effort to shake hands with Israeli players.

At least one Irish player decided to skip the match and leave the team altogether. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu said he refused to play against Israel because of his "personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition of the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region," he added.

It’s unclear if Bazunu had any strong reaction to the terror attack that occurred in Israel nearly three years ago.

Ireland has been one of Israel’s most outspoken critics against the war in Gaza. Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin condemned antisemitism in an interview with Fox News Digital but said Israel’s military response was "absolutely disproportionate."

Ultimately, Irish players voted to play the match after four hours of conversations and a vote, according to Football Association of Ireland (FAI) CEO David Courell.

Israel is set to play each of its Nations League matches in Debrecen. Israel’s Football Association said in a statement that politics and sports should be kept apart.

Ireland went on to win the match, 3-0.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Major League Baseball is eyeing a game at Grand Teton, but federal red tape is slowing down the pitch
item.description: MLB approached the Trump administration about hosting a game in Grand Teton National Park, but the White House says it's not an administration priority.
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball is eyeing its next massive showcase, trading concrete jungles and overpriced stadium beer for pine trees and the iconic peaks of Grand Teton National Park.

Specialty neutral-site games have been massive hits for MLB, but when word leaked that the league was sniffing around federal land, Washington rushed to pump the brakes.

In an official statement, the White House confirmed MLB approached President Donald Trump's administration to ask about hosting a game in a national park, "similar to the Field of Dreams game" in Iowa.

MLB COMMISSIONER UNDERSTANDS WHY TRUMP IS 'INTERESTED' IN MLB CBA NEGOTIATIONS

"This is not a Presidential directive, nor is it being directed by the White House. It’s also not being driven by the Department of Interior," the statement read.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Therefore, this is not a White House or Administration priority."

The White House made sure to add that the National Park Service hasn't granted a single permit, and MLB hasn't finalized a shred of venue planning.

"If the MLB wants to go on site visits of national parks, that is their prerogative," the administration noted.

Washington isn't endorsing a national park game just yet, probably out of fear of taking the heat if a grizzly bear wanders into left field.

And you can’t blame the league for swinging for the fences.

NETFLIX GIVES ELLE DUNCAN ANOTHER MLB SHOWCASE AT FIELD OF DREAMS, BASEBALL FANS HAVE SEEN ENOUGH

Baseball fans ate up the Field of Dreams game in Iowa, the Little League Classic in Williamsport, and the historic trip to Rickwood Field in Alabama.

They even took over Bristol Motor Speedway in 2025.

National Park Service Deputy Director Frank Lands reportedly visited Wyoming to inspect three prospective sites inside Grand Teton.

The White House later claimed Lands wasn't actively scouting baseball diamonds, insisting he was just on a routine tour of several parks.

Still, trying to turn a dusty federal maintenance yard into a million-dollar TV spectacle sounds like an absolute logistical nightmare. You're talking temporary grandstands, massive light towers, crazy traffic bottlenecks, and keeping local grizzly bears, bison and elk out of the dugout.

A project like this triggers environmental reviews, public comment periods, and mountains of paperwork before anyone touches a shovel.

MLB ANNOUNCES EARLIEST EVER OPENING DAY FOR 2027, WRIGLEY FIELD ALL-STAR GAME AMID LABOR UNCERTAINTY

Factor in that MLB’s 2027 special-event schedule is already locked, and 2028 is the absolute earliest we’d see a big-league pop fly framed by the Teton Range.

item.title: Florida Gators may or may not be ‘back,’ but one thing is certain, football is finally fun in The Swamp again
item.description: Jon Sumrall's Florida Gators crushed No. 4 Ole Miss and surged to 8th in the AP Poll, but the new coach says the beast hasn't fully awakened yet.
item.content:encoded:
December 5, 2009.

I remember it like it was yesterday. It was the date of the SEC Championship, the supposed "Game of the Century" in college football.

Florida vs. Alabama. Number one against number two. A rematch of last season's thriller between the two teams and a matchup thought to be a "de facto" national championship game.

FLORIDA GATORS, OLE MISS REBELS FIND THEMSELVES IN GOOD OLD FASHIONED 'RESPECT OFF' AHEAD OF SATURDAY'S GAME

It was also the night the Gators' budding dynasty came crumbling down before our very eyes.

Oh sure, Florida would go on to eviscerate Cincinnati in the Sugar Bowl less than a month later, and they even managed to cobble together a few impressive seasons in the years since.

JAMES MADISON COACH BILLY NAPIER CONTINUES SELF PITY TOUR, REFUSES TO TAKE ACCOUNTABILITY FOR PAST FAILURES

But as far as being the nationally relevant powerhouse they had become under head coaches Steve Spurrier and Urban Meyer in the 90s and 2000s, those days were long gone.

The Gators would stumble their way through myriad coaching searches, hiring flawed candidate after flawed candidate.

If Florida landed a defensive wizard (Will Muschamp), the offense would suffer under his watch.

Conversely, if the Gators nabbed an offensive guru (Dan Mullen), the defense would inevitably fail to live up to their end of the bargain.

FLORIDA GATORS COACH JON SUMRALL SAYS HE WOULDN'T HAVE LEFT TULANE IF HE WASN'T ALLOWED TO COACH PLAYOFF TEAM

And if they happened to get a guy who was a relentless recruiter (Billy Napier), neither side of the ball would look up to snuff.

Big wins were short-lived, usually followed by a cataclysmic event that would tank any shot at a successful season after the fact.

In 2015, the Gators welcomed a top-three Ole Miss team to The Swamp in an eerily similar scenario to Saturday's game, and handled them from the opening whistle.

Just weeks later, rising second-year signal caller Will Grier would be suspended for testing positive for performance-enhancing drugs, and the Jim McElwain era was never able to replicate the magic of those first six games.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL WEEK 4 CONTENDERS, PRETENDERS: TEXAS SURVIVES, MICHIGAN'S KARMA AND COACHES ARE SWEATING

Five years later, during the fog of the COVID-19-shortened season of 2020, Florida had a legitimate championship-level offense under head coach Dan Mullen's tutelage, and even with a porous defense, were able to knock Georgia off its perch and take the inside track to the SEC Championship Game.

A month after their win over their fiercest rival, the Gators lost as a three-touchdown favorite at home to LSU thanks to the now infamous "shoe toss" from defensive back Marco Wilson.

HOW A PODCAST COMMUNITY HELPED RESTORE THE CONTROVERSIAL 'GATOR BAIT' CHANT FOR FLORIDA FOOTBALL TEAM

Mullen was relieved of his duties as head coach less than a year afterwards.

My point is that any time the Gators seemed to gain a foothold in the "we're back" conversation, something would jump up and drag them back to reality.

I'm not sure if Saturday's domination over number four Ole Miss means the Gators are "back," but for the first time in a very long time, the picture is looking clearer than ever.

The offense looks as dangerous as it did six years ago, when that aforementioned 2020 team ran roughshod over a 10-game SEC schedule thanks to the aerial assault provided by Kyle Trask, Kyle Pitts and Kadarius Toney, among others.

And the crazy thing is, this year's offense might be deeper and even more balanced.

Consider the fact that Florida had Eric Singleton Jr., Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton, three of their top four wideouts, all hobbled for large portions of the game, and still put up 52 points and nearly 500 yards of total offense against a top-five SEC team.

That 2020 offense was lethal, but they couldn't run the ball as effectively and certainly didn't have a tailback of Jadan Baugh's magnitude.

The defense was the Achilles heel of that COVID-19-year team, and while this year's unit doesn't look elite, they certainly play a more cohesive brand than their predecessors did in 2020.

Florida fans (myself included) begged on their hands and knees for Lane Kiffin to come to Gainesville.

Ultimately, that didn't work out, and when it was announced that Jon Sumrall was the hire, Gator Nation revolted.

For 24 hours, that is.

After hearing the man speak and seeing the plan he had in place for the orange and blue, many of the Florida faithful started to have hope.

It's early on in the process, but Sumrall and his staff have already started to show proof of concept, winning a road SEC game and then clobbering one of the best teams in the country in back-to-back weeks.

I can't say for certain if Jon Sumrall will ever win anything of significance while coaching the Florida Gators.

This season is only four games old, and it's year one of his tenure.

But with the way things are trending, both on and off the field, it's safe to say football is, at the very least, fun again in The Swamp.

I try to be as objective as possible in my writing, but you can read it for yourself in my bio: I'm an unabashed Florida fan.

This was an article 17 years in the making, and I want to reiterate that the job is far from finished.

The Gators moved all the way up to 8th in the AP Poll on Sunday, their highest position in any poll since the end of the 2020 regular season.

No one is going to hang a banner about where you are ranked in week five, and there are plenty more tests still on the schedule.

This feels different, though.

Will the Gators win an SEC Championship or national title in 2026?

Not likely, but I see the vision from Sumrall and trust this is a sustainable approach to building a consistent winner.

Florida labored in finding an explosive offense outside of a few years with Mullen, so Sumrall went out and hired the best offensive coordinator in the country in Buster Faulkner.

Offensive line play has been downright putrid for large swathes of the last decade and a half, so Sumrall brought offensive line coach and UF alum Phil Trautwein, widely considered the best O-line teacher and recruiter in college football, back to Gainesville.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The man gets it.

Sumrall said in his postgame press conference that the beast hasn't been fully awakened yet, a nod to his comments from his introductory press conference back in December, but he acknowledged that they are getting there.

And if what I'm hearing from those close to the program is true about the recruits in attendance, the beast might be waking up sooner rather than later.

Saying the Gators are "back" feels a bit premature and might be an oversimplification of things, but the fact that they are even in the conversation means things are trending in the right direction.

And that's all this Gator fan, or any of us, can ask for.

item.title: Bill Gates warns artificial intelligence 'powerful enough' to cause 'a billion deaths' if unchecked
item.description: Bill Gates warned on NBC's "Meet the Press" that AI could drive events causing a billion deaths, calling it irresponsible not to require more safeguards.
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could cause "a billion deaths" if left unchecked in the latest push to regulate AI on NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday.

During his interview, Gates, who previously warned that AI could be the "greatest equalizer" or "worst source of injustice" without some level of human regulation, stopped short of answering whether the technology could "end all of humanity" but argued that it could drive events that would lead to significant deaths.

"AI is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths," Gates said. "You know, so even though it’s pretty hard to get to 100%, there’s never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools."

AI EXTINCTION WARNINGS DOMINATE HEADLINES AFTER EX-ANTHROPIC EMPLOYEE'S VIRAL POST

Gates is among several tech giants who have put forth warnings about AI, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Despite this, President Donald Trump has rejected calls to ease back on AI development in an effort to compete with other global powers like China.

Gates disagreed, saying there "absolutely" needed to be more focus on regulation and legislation passed by Congress rather than concerns about global competition.

WATCH: AI SAFETY SCARE SPARKS CAP HILL FIGHT OVER GUARDRAILS: 'CHINA'S GOING TO EAT OUR LUNCH'

"The problem is that the rest of the world is either discounting this or just thinking of this as a competition. And it’s very scary that we don’t have all of the thinkers saying, 'How do we want to shape this?'" Gates said.

When host Kristen Welker compared the situation to limitations around nuclear weapons development between the U.S. and U.S.S.R. during the Cold War, Gates called AI "more difficult," particularly if there is less effort to work with allies.

"And, you know, because it’s cast in this nationalistic, you know, us versus them type thing, you have people who are saying, 'Well, let’s just go full-speed ahead.' It’s completely irresponsible not to require every AI to have these safeguards and monitoring capabilities. And it only is a question of do you do it now?" Gates said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Gates Foundation for comment.

RAND PAUL CLASHES WITH FELLOW REPUBLICAN OVER AI 'KILL SWITCH' AS SENATE GRAPPLES WITH 'TERMINATOR' FEARS

Though Trump has downplayed concerns over AI, some Republicans have called for the government to take action, including Republican National Committee member and Humans First Chairwoman Amy Kremer.

"Even Bill Gates, one of the most influential figures in the history of technology, is now admitting the dangers of artificial intelligence. He warns that AI could drive events causing a billion deaths and that people with ill intent have never held a more powerful weapon. At this point, the only people still denying the reality of the situation are those being paid by Big AI to gaslight the American people," Kremer told Fox News Digital.

However, Laffer Tengler Investments CEO Nancy Tengler called out Gates' comments, claiming that he was belittling his critics with no clear evidence.

"To say that 'there's never been a weapon as powerful' is an absolute statement rich in irony as the [Trump] Administration seeks to keep nuclear weapons out of the hands of the Iranian regime.  The U.S. needs to win the AI race just as we sought to win the arms race during the Cold War," Tengler told Fox News Digital.

In another comment, Julia Cartwright, senior research fellow in law and economics at the American Institute for Economic Research, also offered Fox News Digital a more optimistic view on AI development.

"Economically, what Gates is describing is a catastrophic negative externality. AI is sharply lowering the cost of causing harm, whether that's bioweapons design, cyberattacks or large-scale fraud, while the companies building these tools don't bear the full cost when things go wrong," Cartwright said.

She added, "A way to combat this is clear liability and clear rules of the game, so developers internalize the risks they create. Done right, that doesn't slow American innovation it strengthens it, because firms can build and invest with confidence when they know what's expected of them, and the public can trust what they're building."

item.title: Pope Leo visits site of miracle cures, meets people whose unexplained healings stunned doctors
item.description: Pope Leo XIV prayed at the Massabielle Grotto and planned to meet with miracle cure recipients, sexual abuse victims and the sick during his Lourdes visit.
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV arrived in Lourdes from Paris on Saturday evening for his first-ever visit to the renowned place of miracle cures.

Back in 1858, a 14-year-old peasant girl named Bernadette Soubirous reported having 18 visions of the Virgin Mary at the Lourdes Massabielle Grotto. This ultimately led to her being named a saint.

The pope prayed at the Grotto Saturday night before leading an open-air Mass on the Prairie on Sunday, with hundreds of thousands expected to be in attendance. 

POPE LEO DRAWS STAGGERING 800,000 FAITHFUL TO HEART OF PARIS FOR MASSIVE OUTDOOR MASS

He also planned to meet with bishops, the sick and the support staff.

I spoke with Dr. Alessandro de Franciscis, who recently retired as president of the Lourdes Office of Medical Observation after 17 years of reviewing treatments and possible miracle cures.

He discussed his upcoming meeting with the pope, who he said was visiting Lourdes in the name of purification and healing, including healing from the Church's recent sexual abuse scandals.

JUST 5 MINUTES OF PRAYER COULD HAVE SURPRISING HEALTH BENEFITS, STUDY FINDS

"I think I love him," he told me. "I think he's doing very well (as pope). He's talking of the challenges that we have. You must have heard about his first encyclical letter on artificial intelligence ... all the good that this technology can bring to today's world. He's a guy from Chicago. I love him. We all love him!"

Dr. de Franciscis said the pope would meet with people whose miracle healings were investigated and later recognized by the Church. 

Those include Sister Bernadette Moriau, who was cured of a spinal condition and was able to walk again, and Antonietta Raco, who in 2009 was cured of the severe neurodegenerative disease primary lateral sclerosis.

"He's also going to meet with a young woman (Delizia Cirolli) who was cured when she was only 7 years old of a Ewing's Sarcoma, a right knee cancer, back in the late '70s."

But for Lourdes, as well as for the pope, spiritual and physical healing lead to both minor and major miracles, according to de Franciscis.

He also spoke with me for my new book, "The Angels Among Us," about the hospitaliers, the aptly named "angels of Lourdes," who care for the sick there.

In the book, de Franciscis emphasizes the vital role of the hospitaliers, as well as the fact that much of the healing associated with visits to Lourdes and the Grotto is spiritual and often goes unrecognized — remaining below the radar.

"I think that statistically, these so-called spiritual cures are so, so much more numerous than the physical ones that we know," he said to me from Lourdes, as he eagerly anticipated the pope’s visit.

"People come here to serve, they think they come here to help others — and instead they come out of this experience being so much better," de Franciscis went on.

"And they go back to their work and their lives and their families, and they're so relieved, I would say, they've really changed. So I think this aspect is very, very interesting."

In Lourdes this weekend, in the name of repentance and accountability, the pope also planned to sit down with seven victims of sexual assault committed by clergy of the Church.

item.title: Supersonic Russian jets trigger joint scramble by NATO allies amid Putin 'clowns' jab
item.description: Finnish F/A-18 Hornets and Swedish Gripens scrambled jointly for the first time to intercept supersonic Russian military jets over the Gulf of Finland.
item.content:encoded:
Finnish and Swedish fighter jets scrambled for the first time on Sept. 24 to intercept supersonic Russian military aircraft flying over the Gulf of Finland, marking a major milestone in Nordic defense cooperation amid heightened tensions with Moscow.

The mission also came one day before Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed European warnings about the threat from Moscow in the region and mocked Estonia's new defense minister over the Baltic state's preparations for a potential Russian attack.

Finnish F/A-18 Hornets and Swedish JAS 39 Gripens were scrambled after Russian aircraft were detected in the international airspace, according to the Swedish Armed Forces.

US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS

The Russian formation included a Tu-134 transport plane, a high-altitude, supersonic MiG-31 interceptors designed to detect and engage long-range threats; and Su-30 multirole fighter jets which are designed for air-to-air and air-to-ground combat.

"This is what close cooperation looks like in practice," Maj. Gen. Jonas Wikman, commander of the Swedish Air Force, said in a statement following the joint operation.

"Built over years on trust and strong personal relationships, we can now operate seamlessly together — as air forces, as nations and as Allies."

Concern over Russian military activity along NATO’s eastern flank has grown following a string of airspace violations.

These include Russian drones entering Polish airspace, a Mi-8 helicopter crossing from Kaliningrad into Poland, drones crashing in Romania and Moldova, and armed Russian jets entering Estonian airspace before being intercepted by NATO aircraft on Sept. 18.

BATTLE-TESTED ZELENSKYY SOUNDS CHILLING ALARM ON WHERE PUTIN’S WAR COULD HEAD NEXT

In Estonia, Defense Minister Martin Herem warned that Russia could be capable of using military force against Estonia within a year and argued that Tallinn must determine whether its defenses are sufficient for such a scenario.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal stated that the government is ready to shut down border crossing points on short notice if threat assessments change, according to reports.

Speaking at the St. Petersburg International United Cultures Forum on Friday, Putin pushed back against such warnings.

"Many people in Europe say they expect an attack from Russia and therefore claim they must prepare for war with Russia," Putin said.

"I want to emphasize once again: we are not preparing for military action against Europe. We have no such plans, no basis for them, and, most importantly, no real motive to escalate the situation with Europe."

Putin then mocked Herem's warnings: "As we jokingly say in Russia: 'The circus has left, but the clowns remain.' It is political clowning. ... Clearly, these statements are complete nonsense and absurdity," Putin said, according to EurAsia Daily.

FOREIGN LEADER ON PUTIN’S DOORSTEP SOUNDS ALARM OVER IRAN FUELING MOSCOW’S WAR MACHINE

Estonia sits across the Gulf of Finland from Finland, with the three countries forming part of NATO's increasingly integrated northern and eastern defenses amid concerns about Russian military activity.

Finland formally joined NATO as its 31st member in April 2023, roughly doubling the alliance's land border with Russia. Sweden followed as the 32nd member in March 2024. Estonia, which regained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991, has been a NATO member since 2004.

The Baltic Sea region has also remained on heightened alert following incidents involving gas pipelines, sabotage and hybrid threats since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Reuters has reported.

NATO said in June that it was enhancing protection of its eastern members in the cyber and space domains while helping countries build resilience against what it describes as hostile Russian actions, including cyberattacks, sabotage and airspace violations.

NATO says its military activities along the eastern flank are entirely defensive and that it is "ready, willing and able to defend every Ally."

FINLAND'S STUBB CREDITS TRUMP FOR PUSHING UKRAINE PEACE TALKS WHILE DISMISSING RUSSIAN INVASION FEARS

The alliance has said an attack against any member would be met with a "resounding response."

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte recently underscored Washington's role in the alliance during a visit to Iowa, telling The Associated Press that Putin "knows that the United States and Europe are totally intertwined."

"We have to make sure that we are prepared, we are strong, and he knows it," Rutte said.

"And if he does anything silly, he knows our reaction will be tough," he warned.

European intelligence officials said Sept. 24 that Russia could test NATO's defenses.

Denmark's Defense Intelligence Service assessed the risk of a limited Russian military attack against a NATO country in the coming months as "low but growing" and said Moscow is expected to intensify its hybrid campaign against NATO and the West.

The service said in a statement that a full-scale Russian invasion of a NATO member remains highly unlikely but can no longer be ruled out.

item.title: Popular pantry product can't legally be called peanut butter — here's why
item.description: Skippy must add the word "spread" to its natural peanut butter label due to FDA rules requiring at least 90% peanut content in every single jar.
item.content:encoded:
Peanut butter is a spread by definition, but when the word "spread" appears on a peanut butter jar label, it's most likely satisfying a legal requirement rather than acting as a simple descriptor.

Skippy, a well-known name in the peanut butter world, must label its Natural Peanut Butter Spread as such because it contains palm oil.

Regulations set by the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) state that, in order to be classified as peanut butter, a product must contain at least 90% peanuts — otherwise, the word "spread" needs to be included on the label.

REESE'S FAMILY MEMBER ESCALATES BATTLE WITH HERSHEY OVER CHOCOLATE INGREDIENTS, BLASTS 'PR STUNT'

The Skippy website acknowledges this FDA regulation, saying: "Natural Peanut Butter Spreads can include additional ingredients like palm oil or other oils, which are not hydrogenated."

"These spreads may still contain at least 90% peanuts but include other ingredients that place them outside the standard definition of 'peanut butter,'" the website notes.

It wasn't the smoothest journey to get this regulation set in stone.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Back in 1959, an FDA press release included the findings of a survey which showed that "products labeled ‘peanut butter’ had reduced their peanut content as much as 20 percent by substituting cheaper hydrogenated or vegetable oils for expensive peanuts and peanut oil," according to the FDA.

When manufacturers asked about adding glycerin to peanut butter in order to fight oil separation, the FDA responded by stating that, "if glycerin could be added without rendering the food adulterated, its addition would have to be set forth prominently on the product label."

It became apparent that customers liked peanut butter that spread easily and had a bit of sweetener.

So, in 1961, the FDA proposed a new standard which maintained products consisting of 90 percent peanuts and additional sweeteners would be classified as peanut butter.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Upon this proposal, three peanut butter brands — Skippy, Jif and Peter Pan — began a twenty-week public hearing to argue what peanut percentage the new standard would dictate.

Eventually, the US Appeals Court approved the FDA proposal to set peanut butter standards "at no less than 90 percent for peanuts and no more than 55 percent fat," according to the FDA.

Today, as shoppers browse supermarket shelves stocked with many different variations of peanut butter, taking a closer look at the label could answer an important question: Is it really peanut butter?

item.title: Dan Lanning blasts USC after Oregon's win, as Lincoln Riley officially enters hot seat in LA
item.description: Oregon's Big Ten road win over USC featured Dan Lanning's savage recruiting jab, telling LA players to pick the Ducks if they want to win games.
item.content:encoded:
Week four of the college football season delivered yet again, with wild, last-second upsets in the Big Ten, season-changing wins for programs like Mississippi State and Florida, and high-profile matchups of big-name teams.

Texas A&M-LSU reinforced that the Aggies were wildly overrated, Ole Miss' defense collapsed after the emotional, energetic win over the Tigers the prior weekend, and Iowa pulled off a miracle in yet another bizarre finish at Michigan Stadium.

But one of the most important matchups of the week was in Los Angeles, with the Oregon Ducks coming off a disappointing start to their season and the USC Trojans looking to make a statement at home in their quest to reach the College Football Playoff.

OREGON DUCKS QB DANTE MOORE CARTED OFF THE FIELD AFTER A VICIOUS HIT TO THE HEAD AGAINST USC

A statement was certainly made, but it wasn't by USC. Oregon, a team that was effectively dominated by Oklahoma State a few weeks ago, lost starting quarterback Dante Moore after a brutal, inexcusable hit from an SC linebacker. They fell behind early, had to rely on backup Dylan Raiola, faced questions on their defensive line, and still pulled away in the fourth quarter to save their season with a 41-27 win.

For USC, which brought in the number one recruiting class in the country, hired highly respected former TCU head coach Gary Patterson to run their defense, and brought back one of the top quarterbacks in the country in Jayden Maiava, it was more of the same under head coach Lincoln Riley. And Ducks' head coach Dan Lanning took the opportunity after the game to remind them of it.

In his postgame news conference, Lanning praised the team's response after Moore's devastating, scary injury. He spoke about how prepared Raiola was for the moment, and said his decision-making was impressive after coming off the bench. He explained how his process has changed over time, which led to taking three points right before halftime instead of pushing for a touchdown. At the end of his remarks though, Lanning brought up his record against USC and what he believes it should mean for top LA area players.

"Three wins against these guys," he said. "I guess if you're interested in winning football games and you're from this area, you should go to Oregon. If you want to go to a Chris Brown concert, you should go here."

Ouch. And of course, fair play to Lanning. His team went on the road and deservedly won a game against a tough opponent after their star quarterback suffered a serious injury. Interestingly though, the Oregon social media team never posted the final score of the Oklahoma State game, which was 39-31 Cowboys and should have been far worse.

The Cowboys dominated with nearly 37 minutes of possession while Oregon had just 23 minutes. Moore was 14/29, while the Oregon rushing attack averaged three yards per carry and allowed almost six. Analytics-driven "adjusted" scoring margin based on the statistics and efficiency by both teams was 18 points.

Winning the USC game was a necessary step to save the season, and Oregon established that they're still capable of playing a high-level offensive game, even without Moore. They've also been a decisively better program than USC in recent years. But they've also had little to show for it. In last year's College Football Playoff semifinal, they were obliterated by Indiana 56-22. As the top overall seed in the playoff bracket in 2024-2025, they were down 34-8 to Ohio State at halftime on their way to yet another blowout loss.

If anything, given their immense NIL resources and consistently elite high school and transfer portal recruiting classes, Oregon has underperformed in big games under Lanning.
